zones.what: Lifeboats are mounted at Deck 7; they obstruct the view downward from Decks 8-10, with Deck 8 experiencing the most significant obstruction and the effect diminishing on higher decks.
zones.effect: Looking straight out you see the ocean and horizon clearly, but looking down you see the white fiberglass boat tops instead of water; the sense of height above the waterline is reduced.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to guests who want an unobstructed view in all directions or who enjoy watching the water directly below; doesn't matter to those focused on horizon views or who rarely look down from their balcony.

zones.what: Deck 15 directly above houses the main pool area (Fountain Pool, Movies Under the Stars screen) in the mid to aft sections.
zones.effect: Daytime pool activity, music, movies, and deck parties create noise and vibration from footfall above; activity often continues until late evening.
zones.mattersTo: Significant for light sleepers or anyone wanting a quiet retreat during the day; less important for guests who are out exploring or don't mind ambient resort sounds.

zones.what: Deck 15 directly above houses the World Fresh Marketplace buffet in the forward section.
zones.effect: Breakfast and lunch periods bring chair scraping, footfall, and general dining noise from above; buffet operates long hours starting early morning.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to those sensitive to overhead noise, especially early risers who want to sleep in; minimal concern for guests on the same meal schedule who won't be in the cabin during buffet hours.

zones.what: Deck 16 directly above houses the Sports Court and additional open deck space.
zones.effect: Daytime sports activities and foot traffic create intermittent noise and vibration overhead, though typically less intensive than the main pool deck.
zones.mattersTo: Minor concern for most guests; mainly relevant to very noise-sensitive travelers during daytime hours.

zones.what: The Princess Theater (main showroom) spans Decks 6 and 7 directly below the forward section of Deck 8.
zones.effect: Evening show times bring music, bass vibration, and applause from below; shows typically run twice nightly with the late show ending around 10-11 PM.
zones.mattersTo: Relevant for early-to-bed guests or those sensitive to vibration; not a concern for night owls or those attending the shows themselves.

zones.what: The Club6 nightclub/disco is located on Deck 7 below the aft section of Deck 9.
zones.effect: Late-night bass and vibration from music and dancing can transmit upward, typically from around 10 PM until 2-3 AM on active nights.
zones.mattersTo: Critical for guests who sleep early or are sensitive to bass vibration; irrelevant for late-night partygoers or heavy sleepers.

zones.what: The Royal class has three main elevator banks: forward (near the atrium), mid-ship (port and starboard), and aft; cabins immediately adjacent experience mechanical noise and hallway traffic.
zones.effect: Elevator machinery creates periodic humming and movement sounds; adjacent hallways see concentrated foot traffic as guests come and go, especially during embarkation, mealtimes, and show times.
zones.mattersTo: Matters to light sleepers or those seeking maximum quiet; benefits guests prioritizing convenience who don't mind trading some noise for proximity to vertical transport.

zones.what: These lowest guest decks in the aft section sit relatively close to the propulsion machinery below.
zones.effect: A low-frequency hum or vibration may be noticeable underway, particularly at higher speeds; the sensation is subtle on modern ships but perceptible to sensitive guests.
zones.mattersTo: Relevant for guests highly sensitive to vibration or mechanical noise; most guests either don't notice or quickly acclimate.

zones.what: Bow thrusters used for docking and maneuvering are located in the forward lower section of the hull.
zones.effect: Brief periods of rumbling vibration during docking and undocking, typically early morning in port and evening when departing; lasts only minutes per operation.
zones.mattersTo: Minor inconvenience for very light sleepers in port mornings; most guests are awake or quickly return to sleep after the brief activity.
